title: Peatland ACTION FW02 Field Ecologists Framework
description: NatureScot work to improve our natural environment in Scotland and inspire everyone to care more about it. We work to ensure that all nature in Scotland - our key habitats and landscapes, all our green space and our native species - are maintained, enhanced and bring us benefits. Our priority is a nature-rich future for Scotland and an effective response to the climate emergency. Peatland ACTION funding - from Scottish Government - primarily supports on-the-ground peatland restoration activities and is open for applications from eligible land managers who have peatlands that would benefit from restoration. There are no geographical restrictions or target areas for Peatland ACTION funding. Peatlands are an iconic part of the Scottish landscape and have many benefits for people and nature. Healthy peatlands provide important ecosystem services including storing and sequestering carbon, supporting unique and specialised biodiversity, improving downstream water quality, and regulating water flow to provide natural flood management. In contrast, damage to peatlands reduces or reverses these benefits. For example, degraded peatlands release stored carbon and are a major global source of greenhouse gas emissions. Peatland ACTION is led and funded by Scottish Government and delivered in partnership with NatureScot, Cairngorms National Park Authority, Loch Lomond & the Trossachs National Park Authority, Forestry and Land Scotland, and Scottish Water. Since 2012, Peatland ACTION has set over 66,000 hectares of degraded peatland on the road to recovery, but this effort needs to accelerate rapidly in the coming years to help address the twin crises of the climate emergency and biodiversity loss. The appointed Field Ecologists will work with the Peatland ACTION Technical Team and Project Officers located across Scotland to help support species and ecological survey requirements for Peatland ACTION restoration sites.

Our priority is a nature-rich future for Scotland and an effective response to the climate emergency. Peatland ACTION funding - from Scottish Government - primarily supports on-the-ground peatland restoration activities and is open for applications from eligible land managers who have peatlands that would benefit from restoration. There are no geographical restrictions or target areas for Peatland ACTION funding. Peatlands are an iconic part of the Scottish landscape and have many benefits for people and nature. Healthy peatlands provide important ecosystem services including storing and sequestering carbon, supporting unique and specialised biodiversity, improving downstream water quality, and regulating water flow to provide natural flood management. In contrast, damage to peatlands reduces or reverses these benefits. For example, degraded peatlands release stored carbon and are a major global source of greenhouse gas emissions. Peatland ACTION is led and funded by Scottish Government and delivered in partnership with NatureScot, Cairngorms National Park Authority, Loch Lomond & the Trossachs National Park Authority, Forestry and Land Scotland, and Scottish Water. Since 2012, Peatland ACTION has set over 66,000 hectares of degraded peatland on the road to recovery, but this effort needs to accelerate rapidly in the coming years to help address the twin crises of the climate emergency and biodiversity loss. The appointed Field Ecologists will work with the Peatland ACTION Technical Team and Project Officers located across Scotland to help support species and ecological survey requirements for Peatland ACTION restoration sites.

description: Los 1 - StDeOe.7022 Amphibien: Im Zuge des Donauausbaus Straubing – Vilshofen, Teilabschnitt 1, Straubing – Deggendorf, wird ein Monitoring und Risikomanagement für LBP-Maßnahmen durchgeführt. In diesem Zusammenhang müssen Daten zum Besiedlungserfolg von Amphibien sowie zur Entwicklung der zugehörigen LBP-Maßnahmenflächen erhoben werden. Es handelt sich hierbei um die Arten Knoblauchkröte (Pelobates fuscus) und Laubfrosch (Hyla arborea). Die Vertragslaufzeit erstreckt sich von Januar 2027 – November 2028. Im Rahmen dieser Arbeiten sind die Ergebnisse digital aufzubereiten und ein Erläuterungsbericht sowie eine Fotodokumentation zu erstellen. Los 2 - StDeOe.7023 Offenlandvogelarten: Im Zuge des Donauausbaus Straubing – Vilshofen, Teilabschnitt 1, Straubing – Deggendorf, wird ein Monitoring und Risikomanagement für ausgewählte LBP-Maßnahmen durchgeführt. In diesem Zusammenhang muss 2027 eine Revierkartierungen zur aktuellen Bestandssituation der Offenlandvogelarten Kiebitz (Vanellus vanellus) und Großer Brachvogel (Numenius arquata) durchgeführt werden. Im Zusammenhang des vegetationsbezogenen Monitorings müssen Biotop- und Nutzungstypen, sowie FFH-Kartierungen inkl. Bewertung für die Lebensraumtypen 91E0*, 91F0, 9170 und 6210 durchgeführt werden. Außerdem erfolgt eine Kartierung der Art Lindernia procumbens sowie Arten der Teichried-, Teichboden und Zwergbinsengesellschaften. Im Rahmen des maßnahmenbezogenen Monitorings sind vegetationsökologische Untersuchungen zu, Gehölzaufwuchs, Baumartenzusammensetzung und Störzeiger, sowie weitere standörtliche Erfassungen durchzuführen. Des Weiteren erfolgen bodenkundliche Kartierungen (Fingerprobe) verschiedener LBP-Maßnahmenflächen. Die Vertragslaufzeit erstreckt sich von 2027 bis 2028. Im Rahmen dieser Arbeiten sind die Ergebnisse jährlich digital aufzubereiten und ein Erläuterungsbericht sowie eine Fotodokumentation zu erstellen. title: Research Project on Service Navigation Support for Seniors
description: Title: Research Project on Service Navigation Support for Seniors - 100032783 The Service Navigation Support for Seniors project will have two components. The first component, Component A will review the accessibility of information on support services available to seniors and/or their caregivers across all federal, provincial and territorial (FPT) jurisdictions and to identify common barriers. The objective of Component A is to understand what support services are the most frequently requested across the 14 FPT jurisdictions and why the access rate for information is more elevated, especially as it relates to barriers in accessing them. The second component, Component B, will use the results from Component A and identify, in collaboration with FPT Officials a number of case studies to analyse the mechanisms through which seniors and/or their caregivers learn about and/or access support services aiming to build awareness and improve access to service navigation supports. This would also include policy recommendations for jurisdictions to consider in enhancing service navigation support for seniors.

description: 1.0 INTRODUCTION The Canadian Nuclear Safety Commission (CNSC) has a requirement to build and maintain independent and contracted geoscientific expertise, consistent with international best practice, through an independent scientific advisory group. The group supports the CNSC’s regulatory preparedness by providing independent advice on the long-term management of used nuclear fuel in Canada and by supporting technical reviews of regulatory documentation expected from the Nuclear Waste Management Organization (NWMO) in relation to its Deep Geological Repository (DGR) project. The purpose of this advance contract award notice (ACAN) is to signal the CNSC’s intention to award a contract for these services to: Carleton University 1125 Colonel By Drive Ottawa, ON K1S 5B6 Canada T +1 613 520 2600 www.carleton.ca Before awarding a contract, however, the CNSC would like to provide other suppliers with the opportunity to demonstrate that they can satisfy the requirements set out in this ACAN, by submitting a statement of capabilities within the posting period for this ACAN, which is 15 calendar days. The NWMO initiated the formal regulatory review of their proposed DGR (through an integrated IA, which includes the initial CNSC licence) in early 2026. The ultimate goal is the centralized containment and isolation of Canada’s used nuclear fuel within a deep geological repository. DGRs rely on the host rock and engineered barriers to contain and isolate the wastes from the biosphere for hundreds of thousands to millions of years. Currently, the NWMO has selected the Wabigoon Lake Ojibway Nation - Ignace site in Ontario for the implementation of the project. Currently, the CNSC is developing regulatory preparedness for technical reviews of regulatory documentation expected from the NWMO in support of their DGR project. As part of building and maintaining independent knowledge, the CNSC continues independent and contracted geoscientific research. It is also international best practice for the regulator to have an independent scientific advisory group assist in regulatory preparedness and provide independent advice to the regulator. In 2014, the IAG was formed to respond to this need. Phase I commenced from 2014 to 2018. As part of the Phase II of the IAG took place from 2018 to 2021. The IAG continued in Phase III and IV from 2021 to 2024, and 2024 to 2027, respectively. This SOW outlines the requirements for Phase V of the IAG. 3.0 SCOPE OF WORK AND EXPECTED OUTCOMES The IAG is expected to develop an annual work plan in conjunction with CNSC staff, in-line with the state of the Impact Assessment for the NWMO’s DGR project and consistent with the scope of CNSC’s activities. Based on the tasks identified in the work plan, the IAG will provide independent geoscientific advice to the CNSC related to the long-term management of used nuclear fuel in Canada. The estimated value of the contract is $450,000. Applicable taxes are extra. 5.0 MINIMUM MANDATORY REQUIREMENTS Any interested supplier must demonstrate by way of a statement of capabilities that all members of the group meet the following minimum mandatory requirements: • The supplier must not have been employed by the Nuclear Waste Management Organization (NWMO) within the previous five years. • Academic qualifications of team members shall include graduate degrees from a recognized university (MSc or PhD) in the field of geomechanics, hydrogeology, geology, and geochemistry, geophysics, and any other area deemed necessary by the CNSC as identified during regulatory reviews. • 25 years of experience in field of geomechanics, hydrogeology, geology, and geochemistry • 10 years of experience providing advice in the field of geoscience and radioactive waste management on specific topics including but not limited to deep geological repository, geomechanics, hydrogeology, geology, and geochemistry, geophysics, and any other area deemed necessary by the CNSC as identified during regulatory reviews. 6.0 JUSTIFICATION FOR THE PRE-SELECTED SUPPLIER Carleton University is considered unique because it has an established network of specialized individuals with expertise in the technical fields required for this work, including geomechanics, hydrogeology, geology, geochemistry, geoscience, radioactive waste management, deep geological repositories, site characterization, safety case development, and the long-term safety assessment of geological disposal. While there may be other suppliers with general geoscience expertise, this requirement also requires access to a coordinated group of experts who can provide independent, third-party advice on NWMO submissions related to licensing, while maintaining familiarity with the CNSC’s technical review needs and the Canadian regulatory context. A further key requirement is that the experts must be fully independent from the NWMO. Specifically, they must not have previously performed work for the NWMO and must not have any current or previous relationship with the NWMO as an employee, contractor, or advisor in the past 5 years. This independence requirement significantly limits the availability of alternative sources of supply. Carleton’s established network is therefore uniquely positioned to provide the required breadth of specialized expertise while meeting the strict independence requirement for this contract. These subject matter experts have extensive experience, demonstrated by a track record of providing advice, and conducting research, relevant to the field of nuclear waste disposal. Carleton University has previously provided independent geoscientific advice to the CNSC, demonstrating familiarity with regulatory expectations, review processes, and the provision of objective technical assessments. Lauhdelämpöteho on riippuvainen siitä miten koneita joudutaan käyttämään jäänteon yhteydessä. Siksi mukana vara/lisälämpöratkaisu. DAFM undertakes a significant amount of sampling in nematology to support our agricultural industry and requires the provision of supplemental diagnostics. The successful laboratory will be expected to provide diagnostics on approximately 1500 samples across a range of matrices including soil, peat, and plant material. The diagnostics required will focus on plant parasitic and free-living nematodes, with particular focus, but not limited to, EU Quarantine and Regulated non-Quarantine species. The successful laboratory will be expected to provide results, reports, and advice within designated turnaround times and be accredited in compliance with EU regulations. The provision of this service will assist DAFM in carrying out the required phytosanitary actions to maintain Irelands high plant health status, and to protect our agricultural industry and environment.

title: Infrarakentamisen valvonnan ja tilannekuvan sovelluksen hankinta
description: Infrarakentamisen valvonnan ja tilannekuvan sovelluksen hankinta Kaupunkiympäristön toimiala (KYMP) on toteuttamassa Infrarakentamisen valvonnan ja tilannekuvan sovelluksen hankintaa. Järjestelmä hankitaan ohjelmistopalveluna (SaaS). Sillä tuetaan katujen, puistojen ja muiden yleisten alueiden infrahankkeiden seurantaa valmistelusta takuuajan päättymiseen, erityisesti urakan toteutusvaiheen hallintaa, dokumentointia ja viestintää kenttäolosuhteissa. Järjestelmää käyttävät kaupungin rakennuttajat ja suunnittelijat sekä urakoitsijat ja suunnittelu- ja valvontakonsultit. Käyttäjiä on tavoitetilassa noin 400, ja urakkavaiheessa olevia hankkeita on vuosittain noin 200. Hankinta sisältää ohjelmistopalvelun käyttöoikeudet, ylläpidon ja tuen sekä kiinteähintaisen käyttöönottoprojektin. Ohjelmistopalvelu on toimitettava lopulliseen hyväksymistestaukseen viimeistään 12 kuukauden kuluttua sopimuksen allekirjoittamisesta. Lisäksi hankinta sisältää tarvittaessa erikseen tilattavia koulutus-, jatkokehitys- ja asiantuntijapalveluja. Sopimus on voimassa toistaiseksi. Hankinnan tausta ja kohde on kuvattu tarkemmin liitteessä Hankinnan kohteen kuvaus.,
